activation.details: The widget is enabled at the start of the bar's right section.

payload.actual_result: CPU name (12th Gen i7-1265U after btop's name trimming), load average, memory total/used/available/cached/free, disk list and order (root, swap, home, pkg, log, boot), network interface and IP, and the 'cpu lazy' process order matched btop. Per-core temperatures followed btop's core-to-sensor map. With the pull-down closed the helper used about 0.05% CPU (1 tick in 20 s); with it open about 0.3%, 16 MB resident. Open btop brought up btop floating at 875x600.
payload.expected_result: The helper's figures match btop's for the same moment, and the widget costs little when idle.
payload.limitations: One machine (Intel laptop, coretemp sensors, btrfs subvolumes, Wi-Fi). CPU percentages were compared only roughly because the two samplers do not tick at the same instant. GPU and battery stats were not ported. Two deliberate differences: disk read/write is shown per second while btop prints bytes per update interval (btop_draw.cpp), and subvolumes of one device are folded into one row. Other btop versions may compute differently.
payload.provenance: Firsthand: built and checked on the contributor's own laptop by an AI coding assistant (Claude Code) working at the contributor's request; the assistant inspected the screenshots and logs itself.

root_cause.rationale: This is an optional feature, not a defect; there is no cause to diagnose.

payload.test_method: Ran btop 1.4.7 in a detached 220x60 tmux pane while the helper sampled with detail on, captured the pane, and compared the two. Then enabled the widget in Powerbar, screenshotted the bar and pull-down, launched btop from the widget, and measured the helper's CPU ticks over 20 s with the pull-down closed.
